items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: But primarily Marshall played the clarinet and Ray Perry played the violin, and there was Vernon Alley, the bass player, he was on those records.

ctx.x: But the basic group was made up of Marshall Royal who played clarinet on the date, and Ray Perry

played violin, and some alto. But primarily Marshall played the clarinet and Ray Perry played the violin, and there was Vernon Alley, the bass player, he was on those records. He hadn't been replaced yet, and there was Lionel on the vibes, and Irving Ashby on guitar, and myself on piano.

And one of those dates was a trumpet player who later on left the group. Karl George. He was a very, very fine first trumpet player with a beautiful tone, who had played with Teddy Wilson's very fine, big band. And he had a beautiful sound. He was instrumental --

items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: after Sir Charles Thompson (PHONETIC), who was the first beginner.

ctx.x: His nickname was "Mushmouth." Milt Buckner (PHONETIC) ended up being the regular pianist with the Hampton band, after Sir Charles Thompson (PHONETIC), who was the first beginner. We had a fellow by the name of Vernon Alley (bass) who was a staunch San Franciscoan. He came out of San Francisco for the first and only time in his life with that band and rushed right back home and immediately stayed there for the rest of his life, which he's still living. Of course, he was with our Navy band, of which I was the…
We had a 45-piece military band. I was the leader of the swing band called the Bombadiers, which was a 17-piece band. Vernon Alley was bass player in that particular band.
